transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-19
Time: 15:00 - 15:58 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Connor Li (CSM), Diego Ramos (SE); Jared Moss, Priya Anand, Ellen Park, Tom Rivers (Northshore)
Shared: onboarding runbook link https://redwood.docs/runbooks/northshore, Dedicated sizing spreadsheet (shared in chat)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align implementation owners, hand off runbook, confirm network/VPC access plan, and validate success criteria for the pilot (latency SLOs, cost thresholds, PHI handling).

Topics:
- Deployment mode: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC
- Security/compliance: SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs, data residency
- Networking: VPC peering, egress rules, IP allowlist
- Benchmarks: sample traces, token-distribution, concurrency targets
- Rollout plan and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, i'm Samira from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. we'll keep this tight, 45-60 minutes, want to make sure we hand off ops and get the runbook action items out. Connor will cover the onboarding milestones and Diego will take network/security deep dives.
[00:12] Tom: hey thanks, Tom here. we got a handful of folks, Jared's leading ML questions, Priya for infra, Ellen doing security.
[00:18] Jared: yep thanks. quick note — our immediate goal is a pilot for clinical summarization, throughput around 40 qps peak but fairly spiky, and we need PHI never leaving our VPC for the pilot.
[00:27] Connor: noted. for the PHI constraint we typically recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated with private control plane and VPC peering. there are a couple of variants — Diego give the short version.
[00:35] Diego: yeah so short version: Hosted can't satisfy strict egress controls for PHI. Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated) can be deployed in customer VPC with private networking; or Private on-prem bundle if you need air-gapped. We'll need VPC peering, route tables, and a minimal set of ports for the control-plane. also KMS integration for key wrapping.
[00:50] Priya: when you say private control plane, do you mean you host the control plane in our VPC or you hand us artifacts? we need details for procurement/security.
[00:57] Diego: good call — for Dedicated we provision a private control plane that sits in your AWS account (usually in a customer-managed private subnet) and Redwood agents talk over mutual TLS to the runtime. For the Private on-prem install, we hand over a package. i'll drop the architecture diagram in the runbook. apologies if that was blurred in the doc earlier.
[01:15] Ellen: SOC2 and our internal audit want everthing logged and key rotation. what's your default retention and can we push logs to our SIEM?
[01:22] Connor: yes we have audit logs and can stream them to your SIEM via Kinesis/HTTP forwarder, retention configurable. we also support customer-managed KMS for encrypting model cache and at-rest data. i'll include the SOC2 matrix and integration steps in the packet.
[01:36] Tom: latency — our product team wants p95 under 300ms for short replies; longer generation sometimes okay up to 2s. can Redwood hit that on Dedicated?
[01:44] Diego: depends on model and quantization. for a 2k context with optimized kernels and batching disabled for low-latency routes, Dedicated with A10X-like nodes we've seen p95 of ~180-240ms for gpt-ish open models. we'll need to run a sample with your top prompts and token lengths — can we get sample traces?
[02:05] Jared: yes we'll share a set of five prompt templates and traces, but some contain PHI. can we use redacted traces?
[02:12] Samira: redacted traces are fine; we only need distribution — token lengths, typical prefix reuse so Diego can recommend quantization and batch windows. for PHI we can sign an NDA if needed, but for the pilot redaction should be ok.
[02:25] Priya: network wise — our security team wants explicit IP ranges. do you allow static egress IPs for the runtime endpoints?
[02:31] Diego: we can provide a set of egress IPs for Dedicated and create a peering mapping. with Private the runtime is your control. i'll add the exact /24s to the network checklist.
[02:39] Ellen: SSO: we use Okta and need SCIM user provisioning and SAML for RBAC. also need to enforce least-priv and MFA.
[02:46] Connor: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is role-based, and you can map Okta groups to Redwood roles. we'll send the SSO metadata file and steps.
[02:55] Tom: curious on cost: open models vs smaller custom models — we need unit economics for 100k requests/month and an ops ramp. any ballpark?
[03:04] Samira: i'll share Dedicated vs Hosted cost sheet in the follow up. quick ballpark: Hosted for open models tends to be cheaper to start but Dedicated gives better per-token economics at scale; quantization reduces memory foot and can halve GPU hours for some workloads. we'll include example TCO scenarios in the quote.
[03:22] Jared: regulator question — data residency in EU for EU patients. can you region-pin?
[03:28] Connor: yes region pinning supported; Dedicated capacity can be requested in specific cloud regions. for Private on-prem we obviously keep data in your data center.
[03:34] Priya: about the rollout: what's a safe canary/rollout plan? we want to start at 1% traffic then 10% then full with automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant.
[03:43] Diego: built-in rollouts support canary and A/B. policy can be traffic-percent based and we have automatic fallback to smaller models or Hosted if Dedicated capacity is constrained. We'll help author a runbook for the step-up schedule.
[03:57] Jared: perf tests — do you have a harness we can run or do we run locally?
[04:03] Diego: we have a benchmark harness (we'll share repo link) that can run from your infra to our endpoints using mutual TLS keys. for private installs we can run runs in your environment. expect to run 30-60 minute test windows to capture warm-cache behavior.
[04:18] Samira: i'll include the harness link in the notes.
[04:22] (short pause)
[04:30] Priya: procurement — timeline: procurement requires an SOW, network attachment doc, and security package. how quickly can you produce those?
[04:37] Connor: SOW draft and network attachment usually same week; security package (SOC2, pen test, vulnerability statements) within 48 hours of request. we'll attach certs and our standard DPA.
[04:46] Ellen: we do need encryption at rest using our KMS. you mentioned customer-managed KMS — how is key rotation handled?
[04:53] Diego: we support BYOK via AWS KMS. rotation policies are controlled on your side; Redwood will accept encrypted keys for stores and never persist plaintext keys. we'll provide the integration steps in the runbook.
[05:05] Tom: okay let's talk pilot success criteria to put in the SOW: 1) p95 latency < 300ms for short responses for 90% of calls; 2) cost per 1k tokens under target X (we'll define); 3) no PHI exfiltration and SIEM ingestion verified; and 4) stable throughput at 30 qps for 30 minutes.
[05:27] Samira: that's a good list; we'll put it in the SOW. Jared and Priya are owners for providing traces and network access.
[05:34] Jared: yes we'll get the traces and a redacted dataset.
[05:38] Priya: timeline constraints — infra change freeze starting 2027-06-10 for a month; we need to be live before that. possible?
[05:46] Diego: timeline might be tight but doable. we should aim to have network peering and SSO validated by 2027-06-07 to leave buffer.
[05:54] Connor: action items and due dates will be in the follow-up email.
[06:00] (crosstalk)
[06:05] Samira: quick callouts — we'll run a small, 2-node Dedicated pilot for initial validation, then scale. recommended node types and quantization profiles will be in Diego's note after he sees traces.
[06:17] Diego: one more technical note — prefix caching (K V cache) will reduce token cost if there's lots of repeated prefixes in prompts; we can configure automatic prefix caching but if you have PII concerns we can limit cache persistence or encrypt caches with customer KMS.
[06:35] Ellen: that caching detail helps. from the audit side we need to know which prompts get cached and TTLs.
[06:42] Diego: yes TTLs are configurable per-route. we'll document default TTLs and how to change them.
[06:50] Tom: any red flags on our infra notes so far?
[06:56] Priya: just that we need exact IPs and the peering runbook.
[07:00] Samira: okay quick recap and decisions: Dedicated in customer VPC for pilot; runbook will be updated with network and SSO steps; Redwood to run benchmark harness with redacted traces; procurement docs to be drafted and shared.
[07:13] Connor: i'll take SOW and security package action. Diego takes the network runbook update. Samira sends pricing and next steps. Jared and Priya provide traces and network contacts.
[07:24] Jared: any questions about data retention for trace logs? we want to purge after testing window.
[07:29] Connor: yes we'll set retention and provide deletion proof; add that to the SOW.
[07:35] Samira: place to upload artifacts: we'll use the shared S3 invite and runbook link; i'll include instructions.
[07:41] Ellen: do you support third-party model vetting — we might want to run a model risk check.
[07:47] Diego: we can run quality checks and regression tests tied to your eval set. Redwood Optimize will surface regressions and you can tie alerts to quality thresholds. small caveat — some names in our internal docs might be mis-typed, so we'll walk through the test harness together.
[07:58] Tom: good. any blockers?
[08:00] Priya: procurement timeline slightly blocker but manageable.
[08:03] Samira: final quick logistics: next touch is a 30-minute network handoff Thurs 2027-05-20 at 16:00 UTC — is that okay?
[08:11] Priya: yes that's fine.
[08:13] Jared: works for me.
[08:15] Samira: perfect. we'll send calendar and artifacts. thanks everyone.

Closing notes:
- Links shared: onboarding runbook https://redwood.docs/runbooks/northshore, Dedicated sizing spreadsheet (chat attachment), benchmark harness repo (private link shared post-call)
- Follow-up email to include: SOW draft, security package, Dedicated pricing, and calendar invites for the VPC handoff and benchmark window.

End of transcript.
